# Version history

- 2026-10-25: first draft, written from the analysis sessions of 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-25.
- 2026-10-27: the 1.0 run was repeated under the correct model and is now the benchmark of the clustering and parts comparisons, and its phylum-level flags were checked with BLAST; the run time of a complete run was added (walltime and CPU time summed over tasks).
- 2026-10-26: added the `--cluster_identity 0.99` run (under the correct model) and a per-representative measure of the flags kept, because the member-weighted genus-level share is dominated by a few large clusters.

# Summary

The default `--cluster_identity 1.0` run of nf-core/taxmarker on all 1,118,534 bacterial 16S sequences of GTDB release 232 places 239,806 sequences and needs 414.6 GB for each of 25 placement folds, 19.8 hours of fold walltime in all (about 10 hours with two folds at a time).
We asked how much of that cost can be removed, and what is lost.

- **Clustering at 0.97** cuts the placed sequences to 92,406, one fold to 135.6 GB and 4.5 minutes, and a complete run to 5.8 hours of task walltime (@tbl-funnel, @tbl-runtime).
  It finds 84-91% of the flags of the 1.0 run at phylum to family level, 72% at genus level and 37% at species level; counted per distinct representative the genus and species shares are 66% and 29% (@tbl-clustering, @tbl-099).
  Below 0.97 the tree barely shrinks, because every taxon keeps at least one representative (@tbl-sweep).
- **A complete run** costs 30.9 hours of task walltime and 242.5 hours of CPU time at 1.0, 6.8 and 35.2 at 0.99, and 5.8 and 28.7 at 0.97 (@tbl-runtime).
- **Clustering at 0.99** places 103,225 sequences, needs 152.5 GB and 5.6 minutes per fold, and finds more species-level flags than 0.97 (42% of the representatives of the 1.0 flags against 29%) and the same share at the other ranks (@tbl-099).
- **The raxtax prefilter** should stay on.
  Without it SATIVA flags 6,222 more sequences, and among the flags that BLAST can judge most of the extra ones point at the declared taxon (@tbl-raxtax).
- **Dividing the tree for placement** does not recover what clustering loses.
  Leave-one-out inside parts of the tree finds 30-65% of the whole-tree flags at phylum to family level and 6-7% at genus level, whether the part has 4 or 50 outgroups (@fig-methods).
  A backbone of one representative per genus finds 71-86% at phylum to family level and 35% at genus level (@fig-methods).
  Only the memory use falls (about 55 GB per fold for the backbone).
- **The model used by sativa-epang** was not that of the reference tree in the first runs (nf-core/taxmarker#64, fixed in #67).
  Rerunning under the correct model leaves memory and time unchanged (@tbl-fixedmodel).
  At 0.97 it changes 17-18% of the flags, mostly ones with a low placement weight.
  At 1.0 it changes 34-38% (40-45% at genus and species level), and the flags that change have a median placement weight of 1.0.
  Flags at genus and species level are therefore sensitive to the model.
  Repeating one 0.97 fold changed the top placement of 1.5% of its queries, all of them ties between equally weighted edges, and ties are 3-5 times as common at 1.0, so placement noise is small but not zero.

# Introduction

taxmarker places each sequence back into a reference tree with sativa-epang after removing it from the tree (leave-one-out), and flags it if the placement disagrees with the declared taxonomy.
The memory use of the placement grows with the number of sequences in the tree.
For a database of hundreds of thousands of sequences, the memory a single placement job needs is the limit on what can be run.
There are three ways to make the tree smaller or the placement lighter: cluster the input first (`--cluster_identity`), remove sequences with a prefilter (raxtax), or place against parts of the tree.
This report measures the first two on one large run and tests the third without building it into the pipeline.
The small injected test sets of `taxmarker-mislabel-tests.qmd` are a different question and are not used here.

# Materials and Methods

## Input and runs

All runs used the 1,118,534 bacterial sequences in GTDB's `ssu_all_r232.fna.gz` [@gtdb], with `--upstream GTDB` weights and the same tree search settings and seed.
The runs differ in `--cluster_identity` (1.0, 0.99 and 0.97) and in whether raxtax was on (`--skip_raxtax`).
The reference tree was searched by the divided tree search of nf-core/taxmarker#66 and the placement ran in 25 folds, one per job.
Runs were done on a shared server with 128 cores.
A run is named by its output directory below: `bac-ssu-r232-1` (identity 1.0, the first run), `bac-ssu-r232-1-0.97`, `bac-ssu-r232-1-0.97-skip_raxtax`, `bac-ssu-r232-1-0.97-fixedmodel`, `bac-ssu-r232-1-0.99-fixedmodel` and `bac-ssu-r232-1-fixedmodel` (identity 1.0 under the correct model).
The code of the first runs is tagged `run/taxmarker-bacteria-2026-10` in the fork and that of the three `fixedmodel` runs `run/taxmarker-bacteria-fixedmodel-2026-10`, which adds the change of nf-core/taxmarker#67.
The tables use the `fixedmodel` runs, except where a section says that it used the first runs.

A flag has a mismatch rank, the highest rank at which the declared and the proposed lineage differ: 2 phylum, 3 class, 4 order, 5 family, 6 genus, 7 species.
SATIVA flags and raxtax flags are counted separately; raxtax flags are all at genus level.

## Flags kept under clustering

At 0.97 a sequence that is not a representative is not placed.
It counts as caught if its representative (same cluster and taxon) is flagged by SATIVA or raxtax, because a cluster member inherits the verdict of its representative (`scripts/large/proxy.py`).
The share of the flags of the 1.0 run (the `fixedmodel` run) found at 0.97 is therefore reported three ways: among the sequences placed in both runs, over all flags with this inheritance, and as the share of distinct representatives that are flagged (`scripts/large/reps.py`).
The second counts member sequences, so a few large clusters weigh heavily: at genus level the ten largest representatives carry 6,074 of the 8,713 flags of the 1.0 run and one carries 2,325.
The third counts each (cluster, taxon) pair once and is the more stable measure.

## Run time

The runs were resumed several times, so the elapsed time of a launch says little about the cost of a run.
The cost of a complete run is the sum over its tasks of the walltime (`realtime` in the Nextflow trace) and of the CPU time (walltime times `%cpu`).
A cached task keeps the figures of the task that ran, so the last successful launch of a run lists every task of a complete run once (`scripts/large/runtimes.py`).
Tasks that failed or were aborted in any launch are summed separately.
CPU time is the CPU actually used, not the cores allocated.

## BLAST check

Flags were checked against the NCBI RefSeq 16S database (`blastn`, BLAST 2.17.0 [@blast]) with the original, ungapped sequences.
Alignment-derived sequences are 10-30 nt shorter and gave false weak hits.
A top hit with at least 97% identity and 90% coverage counts as strong.
The genus of a strong hit gives a lineage through the GTDB taxonomy of the same run, and the hit is compared with the declared taxon and the proposed taxon at the flag's rank.
Sequences with only weak hits cannot be judged.
At species rank the check is unreliable because 16S sequences of related species are nearly identical, so species-level flags are not judged.

## Divided placement tests

Neither divided test is in the pipeline.
Both ran sativa-epang by hand, all four stages in one directory, on a sample of the tree.

- **Parts.** TREEDIVIDE splits the 240k tree into 472 parts of at most 2,000 tips.
  40 parts were sampled, stratified by size with the root part excluded, holding 20,329 own tips (13 parts of 500 tips or more hold 88% of them).
  Each part is placed with the part's own reference tree and model, 4 or 50 outgroups from the rest of the tree and 3 representatives per closed child, and flags are counted for the part's own tips only, at a placement weight of at least 0.5 (`scripts/large/dnc_prep.py`, `dnc_run.sh`, `dnc_cmp.py`, `cmp2.py`).
- **Backbone.** One tree of 46,682 tips: for each of the genera the weightiest sequence that no whole-tree run flagged (18,367 representatives), the 14,315 candidates (every sequence with a whole-tree SATIVA flag at ranks 2-6) and 14,000 control sequences drawn at random from those without a whole-tree flag.
  The 240k tree was pruned to these tips, with no new tree search, and sativa-epang ran on it with the model of the full tree and the same minimum weight (`scripts/large/bb_prep.py`, `bb_run.sh`, `bb_cmp.py`).

The benchmark of the parts test is the set of SATIVA flags of the `bac-ssu-r232-1-fixedmodel` run on the sampled tips.
The backbone was built around the flags of the first 1.0 run (`bac-ssu-r232-1`), its candidates and controls were chosen from them, and its benchmark is that run.

## Scripts and data

The scripts are in `scripts/large/` and read the run directories on the server by absolute path, so they document the analysis and do not run elsewhere.
The tables in `data/large_*.tsv` hold their output, with the script in the last column.
`scripts/large/` also has the BLAST helpers (`sr_prep.py`, `srblast.sh`, `sr_sum.py`, `q.py`, `orig.py`, `miss*.py`, `r2*.py`, `sumblast*.py`) and the clustering sweep (`sweep.sh`).

# Results

## Size and cost

```{r tbl-funnel}
#| label: tbl-funnel
#| tbl-cap: Size and cost of the bacterial run at three cluster identities, all under the correct model. Placement folds ran 3 at a time at 0.97 and 0.99 and 2 at a time at 1.0. Time of one placement fold is the median over the 25 folds.

read_tsv("data/large_funnel.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(Metric = metric, Unit = unit, `1.0` = `id_1.0`, `0.99` = `id_0.99`, `0.97` = `id_0.97`) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Clustering at 0.97 removes 53% of the representatives and 61% of the placed sequences, since profile cover removes a larger share of what is left (@tbl-funnel).
Memory of one placement fold falls to 0.33 of its value for 0.39 of the sequences, and time to 0.09.
Memory per fold grows roughly as the number of tips to the power 1.06 from 0.97 to 0.99 and 1.17 from 0.97 to 1.0.
Time per fold grows faster than memory: 4.5 minutes at 92,406 sequences, 5.6 at 103,225 and 47.5 at 239,806; the folds ran with different numbers at a time on a shared server, so the steps are not strictly comparable.
At 1.0 the 25 folds took 19.8 hours of walltime, about 10 hours with two at a time; at 0.97 three ran at a time with 300 GB each and the first 0.97 run took 2 h 17 min from start to end.
The scoring step (`loo-score`) needs 35.9 GB at 92,406 sequences, 1.1 GB at 103,225 and 11.3 GB at 239,806 (2.5 GB in the first 1.0 run), which is unexplained and not a function of the number of sequences.

```{r tbl-runtime}
#| label: tbl-runtime
#| tbl-cap: Cost of a complete run at three cluster identities, summed over all tasks, with the number of representatives after clustering and after the raxtax prefilter. All three runs used the correct model. Failed tasks are not in the sums.

read_tsv("data/large_runtimes.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(Metric = metric, Unit = unit, `1.0` = `id_1.0`, `0.99` = `id_0.99`, `0.97` = `id_0.97`) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

A complete run at 1.0 costs 30.9 hours of task walltime and 242.5 hours of CPU time, against 5.8 and 28.7 at 0.97: 5.3 times the walltime and 8.5 times the CPU time (@tbl-runtime).
The placement folds are 64% of the walltime at 1.0 and a third at 0.99 and 0.97, where the tree search is as large (@tbl-runtime).
The first runs under the wrong model cost 28.6 hours at 1.0 and 5.8 at 0.97, close to the 30.9 and 5.8 under the correct one (@tbl-runtime).
The tasks that failed in the first 1.0 run (killed at the memory limit, and a failed alignment step) used another 6.2 hours; those of the 1.0 rerun used 0.6.
The elapsed time depends on how many tasks fit on the server at once: at 1.0 only two folds of 415 GB fit at a time, so the folds alone took about 10 hours.
The tree search, clustering, raxtax and alignment of the 1.0 rerun were taken from the first 1.0 run through `-resume`, so the sums count them once.

```{r tbl-sweep}
#| label: tbl-sweep
#| tbl-cap: Representatives (one per cluster and taxon) at several cluster identities, on the input of the 1.0 run after weighting.

read_tsv("data/large_sweep.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(`Cluster identity` = cluster_identity, Representatives = representatives) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Most of the reduction happens between 1.0 and 0.97, and 0.97 to 0.9 removes 6% of the representatives (@tbl-sweep).
The floor is the number of distinct taxa in the input, 96,125, because every taxon keeps a representative.
A value below 0.97 therefore saves little and loses more flags.
The 0.99 point, 164,357 representatives, was run; it gives 103,225 placed sequences against 92,406 at 0.97.

## What clustering does to the flags

```{r tbl-clustering}
#| label: tbl-clustering
#| tbl-cap: Flags of the 1.0 run (correct model) found at 0.97 (correct model). The first two columns count the 89,538 sequences placed in both runs; the last two count all flags, with a cluster member inheriting the verdict of its representative.

read_tsv("data/large_clustering_recall.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(
    Rank = rank,
    `Flags at 1.0 (placed in both)` = `flags_1.0`,
    `Also flagged at 0.97 (%)` = pct_flagged_in_both_runs,
    `Flags at 1.0 (all)` = `flags_1.0_all`,
    `Caught at 0.97 (%)` = `pct_caught_at_0.97`
  ) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Flags at phylum to family level mostly stay (84-91% caught), at genus level 72% do and at species level 37% (@tbl-clustering); counted by distinct representatives the genus-level share is 66% and the species-level share 29% (@tbl-099).
Over all ranks, 22,060 of the 43,127 flags (51%) are caught.
The first 1.0 run, placed under the wrong model, gave 83-93% at phylum to family level, 56% at genus and 39% at species level against the first 0.97 run (`data/large_clustering_recall_first_1.0.tsv`), so the shares are the same within a few points except at genus level, where a few large clusters decide the member-weighted share.
Species-level flags depend on which sister species are in the tree, so they change when sequences are removed.

**BLAST of the phylum-level flags.**
All 3,903 phylum-level flags of the 1.0 rerun were checked.
The 3,197 that the first 1.0 run also flagged kept their result and the 706 new ones were run (`scripts/large/r2new.py`, `r2sum_new.py`).
The categories say what happened to the flagged sequence at 0.97 (@tbl-phylumblast).

```{r tbl-phylumblast}
#| label: tbl-phylumblast
#| tbl-cap: BLAST top hit of the 3,903 phylum-level flags of the 1.0 rerun, by what happened to the sequence at 0.97, and the phylum the hit lies in. Declared and proposed refer to the flag. Weak hits are below 97% identity or 90% coverage.

read_tsv("data/large_blast_phylum.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  select(Category = category, Declared = declared_phylum, Proposed = predicted_phylum, Both = both,
         Other = third_phylum, `Genus unknown` = genus_unknown, `Weak hit` = weak_hit, `No hit` = no_hit, Total = total) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Of the 3,903 flags, 1,502 have only weak hits.
For the flags with a strong hit:

- Flags found in both runs were mostly right: the hit lay in the phylum the flag proposed for 1,091 of 1,190 (@tbl-phylumblast).
- Flags found only at 1.0 were mostly wrong: for the 288 whose representative was not flagged at 0.97, the hit lay in the declared phylum for 278.
  83 of those representatives were also flagged in the 1.0 run, so the placement depends on the tree, a pattern consistent with long-branch attraction that has not been tested.
- 84 flags that look right had no representative flagged, about 6% of the phylum-level flags that look right.

The 706 flags that are new in the rerun are mostly wrong: of the 607 with a strong hit, 506 lie in the declared phylum and 97 in the proposed one.
The rerun as a whole has the same mix as the first run (1,436 strong hits in the proposed phylum against 793 in the declared one; first run 1,418 against 794), so the model change swapped flags without changing the share that look wrong.

At phylum level 0.97 thus dropped many flags that look wrong and missed few that look right.
At genus and species level the loss is larger and cannot be judged this way.
For species with many sequences (*Escherichia coli*, *Klebsiella pneumoniae*, *Staphylococcus aureus*, *Salmonella enterica*, *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*) more than 99% of the sequences not flagged in the rerun had a top hit in the expected genus (99.4-100%; `scripts/large/sp_new.py`).

The choice of cluster identity is therefore a choice between two kinds of error.
At 1.0 more genus and species mislabels are found, but many phylum-level flags are artefacts that remove correctly labelled sequences.
At 0.97 more correctly labelled sequences stay, but about a third of the genus-level and two thirds of the species-level flags are not found.

## Identity 0.99

```{r tbl-099}
#| label: tbl-099
#| tbl-cap: SATIVA flags by mismatch rank in the 0.97 and 0.99 runs under the correct model, and the share of the flags of the 1.0 run (correct model) kept. Members = share of the flagged sequences of the 1.0 run caught directly or through the representative of their cluster; representatives = share of the distinct representatives of those sequences that are flagged (SATIVA or raxtax).

runs <- read_tsv("data/large_clustering_runs.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
runs %>%
  filter(run != "0.97") %>%
  transmute(
    Rank = rank,
    Run = sub(" fixed model", "", run),
    `1.0 flags` = `whole_tree_flags_1.0`,
    `Flags in run` = sativa_flags_in_run,
    `Members (%)` = members_caught_pct,
    `Representatives` = distinct_reps,
    `Representatives (%)` = reps_flagged_pct
  ) %>%
  arrange(Rank, desc(Run)) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

At 0.99 the run has 15,722 SATIVA flags against 11,757 at 0.97, with 8,575 shared, and the extra flags are mostly at species level (6,854 against 3,713) (@tbl-099).
Memory and time per fold rise by 12% and 24% (152.5 GB, 5.6 minutes).
The share of representatives flagged is the same at ranks 2-6 (91-92% at phylum, 64-66% at genus level) and higher at species level (42% against 29%).
The flags found only in one of the two runs have a median placement weight of 1.0 for 0.99 and 0.61 for 0.97, so the extra flags at 0.99 are not weak ones.
The member-weighted shares are less stable than the representative shares: at genus level they are 72% for 0.97 and 56% for 0.99, although the representative shares are 66% and 64%.
The difference comes from a handful of large clusters whose representative is or is not flagged, so a member-weighted genus-level share should not be read to a few percentage points.

## With and without the raxtax prefilter

Both runs of this section are among the first runs, placed under the wrong model.
At 0.97 with `--skip_raxtax` 99,166 sequences are placed instead of 92,406, SATIVA flags 17,812 instead of 11,590 and one placement fold needs 145.7 GB instead of 135.6 GB.
raxtax flagged 14,564 sequences in the run with raxtax, all at genus level.
Of these, 7,390 fail profile cover and are never placed, so SATIVA could not have flagged them.
The other 7,174 are placed when raxtax is skipped, and SATIVA flags 5,329 (74%) of them.

The two runs also differ on the other sequences.
Of the 91,992 sequences placed in both, 8,861 flags are shared, 2,575 are found only with raxtax and 3,622 only without it.

```{r tbl-raxtax}
#| label: tbl-raxtax
#| tbl-cap: BLAST top hit of flags by where it lies, for flags found only without raxtax, for a random 1,500 of the flags found in both runs, and for raxtax flags that SATIVA does not confirm. Declared and proposed refer to the taxon at the flag's rank. Species rank (1,960 flags only without raxtax) is not judged.

read_tsv("data/large_raxtax_blast.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(rank != 7) %>%
  mutate(set = recode(
    set,
    new_without_rax = "only without raxtax",
    both_sample = "in both runs (random 1,500)",
    rax_notflagged = "raxtax flag, no SATIVA flag"
  )) %>%
  select(Set = set, Rank = rank, Declared = declared, Proposed = predicted, Both = both, Other = other,
         `Genus unknown` = genus_unknown, `Weak or no hit` = weak_hit, Total = total) %>%
  kable()
```

Among the flags found only without raxtax, a strong hit mostly lies in the declared taxon at ranks 2-5 (@tbl-raxtax).
For the flags found in both runs it is the opposite: at phylum level 361 of 432 strong hits are in the proposed phylum and 41 in the declared one.
Leaving sequences with a clearly wrong label in the tree therefore creates flags on other sequences that are mostly wrong.

The flags raxtax makes and SATIVA does not confirm are not all right either.
Of 1,845 such sequences 1,348 have only weak hits; of the 468 with a strong hit the hit lies in the declared genus for 376 and in the genus raxtax proposed for 37.
The prefilter should therefore stay on.
Not checked against NCBI: the 2,575 flags found only with raxtax and the 5,329 raxtax flags that SATIVA confirms.

## Divided leave-one-out

Placing each part of the tree separately cuts the memory, but a part cannot propose a taxon that is not in it.
A part ran in 10 seconds to 4 minutes.

```{r tbl-divided}
#| label: tbl-divided
#| tbl-cap: Whole-tree flags of the 1.0 rerun on the 20,329 tips of 40 sampled parts, and how many were flagged again by the part-wise placement with 4 and 50 outgroups. Part-wise flags that the whole tree did not make are in the last two columns.

read_tsv("data/large_divided.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(
    Rank = rank,
    `Whole-tree flags` = whole_tree_flags,
    `Flagged again, 4 outgroups` = recalled_4_outgroups,
    `%, 4` = round(100 * recalled_4_outgroups / whole_tree_flags),
    `Flagged again, 50 outgroups` = recalled_50_outgroups,
    `%, 50` = round(100 * recalled_50_outgroups / whole_tree_flags),
    `Only part-wise, 4` = partwise_only_4,
    `Only part-wise, 50` = partwise_only_50
  ) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

On these tips 3,808 sequences (19%) have a whole-tree flag in the 1.0 rerun, and the part-wise placement flags 1,140 (4 outgroups) or 1,171 (50 outgroups), of which 899 or 913 are also whole-tree flags (@tbl-divided).
Against the first 1.0 run the shares were the same within 5 points at every rank (`data/large_divided_first_1.0.tsv`).
Fifty outgroups barely help.
The two analyses of where the proposed genus and species lie were made on the flags of the first 1.0 run, so their counts differ slightly from the table.
The cause is that for 294 of the 374 genus-level whole-tree flags (79%) the genus the sequence is moved to is not in its part at all; where it is, the part flags 27 of 80.
At species level the proposed species is in the part for 2,290 of 2,453 flags, yet only 523 are reproduced, so species flags depend on the wider tree.
The flags only the part-wise placement makes are 94-95% species-level; their median placement weight is 0.74-0.83 and they have not been checked by BLAST.
Of the 146 phylum-level flags of the rerun with a strong hit that the part-wise placement (4 outgroups) flags, 69 look right and 77 wrong; it drops 52 right and 234 wrong ones.

## Backbone

A second stage that places only the sequences flagged inside their part against a backbone could supply the destination outside the part.
The test above puts every candidate (all whole-tree flags at ranks 2-6 of the first 1.0 run) on one tree of 46,682 tips with a backbone of genus representatives.
It was not repeated against the 1.0 rerun, because the candidates and controls were chosen from the first run's flags and the rerun's flags outside them are not in the tree.

```{r tbl-backbone}
#| label: tbl-backbone
#| tbl-cap: Whole-tree flags of the first 1.0 run at ranks 2-6 (candidates) and how many were flagged again in the backbone tree, at any rank, at the same rank, and with the same proposed taxon at that rank.

read_tsv("data/large_backbone.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(
    Rank = rank,
    `Whole-tree flags` = whole_tree_flags,
    `Flagged again` = flagged_again,
    `%` = round(100 * flagged_again / whole_tree_flags),
    `Same rank` = same_rank,
    `Same proposed taxon` = same_predicted_taxon
  ) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

The backbone finds 71-86% of the flags at ranks 2-5 and 35% at genus level (@tbl-backbone); with the same proposed taxon it is 50-71% at ranks 2-5 and 24% at genus level.
It also makes flags the whole tree did not: 659 of the 14,000 control sequences (4.7%; 72 at phylum level, 244 at genus and 327 at species level) and 654 of the 18,367 backbone representatives (3.6%).
Memory is about 55 GB per fold.
Placement took 3 h 9 min for 25 folds with 4 folds at 8 threads at a time, while the server was shared, so the time is not comparable with the other runs.

```{r fig-methods}
#| label: fig-methods
#| fig-cap: "Share of the whole-tree flags found again by each way of reducing the tree, by mismatch rank. Clustering at 0.97 and divided placement (40 sampled parts) are measured against the 1.0 rerun; the backbone (one tree of 46,682 tips) against the first 1.0 run. Clustering at 0.97 counts flags caught directly or through the representative of the cluster."
#| fig-height: 4

cl <- read_tsv("data/large_clustering_recall.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(rank, method = "clustering 0.97", pct = `pct_caught_at_0.97`)
dv <- read_tsv("data/large_divided.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(recalled_4_outgroups, recalled_50_outgroups), names_to = "method", values_to = "n") %>%
  transmute(rank, method = recode(method, recalled_4_outgroups = "parts, 4 outgroups", recalled_50_outgroups = "parts, 50 outgroups"),
            pct = 100 * n / whole_tree_flags)
bb <- read_tsv("data/large_backbone.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(rank, method = "backbone", pct = 100 * flagged_again / whole_tree_flags)

bind_rows(cl, dv, bb) %>%
  filter(rank <= 6) %>%
  ggplot(aes(factor(rank), pct, fill = method)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "Mismatch rank (2 phylum ... 6 genus)", y = "Whole-tree flags found again (%)", fill = NULL)
```

No design recovers the genus-level flags (@fig-methods).
Clustering at 0.97 finds more than both divided designs at every rank (84-91% against 30-86% at ranks 2-5, and 72% against 35% or less at genus level), and its cost is the lowest of the three.

## The model of sativa-epang

Until nf-core/taxmarker#67, `SATIVAEPANG_LOOTASKS` and `SATIVAEPANG_LOOSCORE` did not receive the reference tree's model file, so sativa-epang placed under a plain `GTR+G` while the tree had been searched under `GTR+FO+G4m`.
The first runs were placed that way.
The 0.97 and the 1.0 runs were repeated under the correct model, and the 0.99 run was made under it.
The two manual tests ran every stage in one directory and so used the right model.

```{r tbl-fixedmodel}
#| label: tbl-fixedmodel
#| tbl-cap: SATIVA flags of the first run and the rerun under the correct model, by mismatch rank, at cluster identity 0.97 and 1.0. The same sequences were placed and the same raxtax flags were made in each pair (14,564 at 0.97 and 19,113 at 1.0).

fm <- read_tsv("data/large_fixedmodel.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
fm %>%
  transmute(
    Identity = identity,
    Rank = rank,
    `Before` = flags_old_model,
    `After` = flags_fixed_model,
    `In both` = both,
    `Same proposed taxon` = same_predicted_taxon,
    `Only before` = only_old,
    `Only after` = only_new
  ) %>%
  kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

At 0.97 SATIVA flags go from 11,590 to 11,757 (+1.4%), with 9,586 in both, 2,004 only before and 2,171 only after (@tbl-fixedmodel).
At 10% (phylum) to 37% (species) of the flags before are not found after, and a similar share is new.
The flags found in both runs have a median placement weight of 1.0, the flags found in only one run 0.51, and 1,157 of the 2,004 flags only before and 1,254 of the 2,171 only after have a weight below 0.6.
So at 0.97 the high-confidence flags are stable and those near the threshold move.

At 1.0 SATIVA flags go from 40,587 to 43,127 (+6.3%), with 26,599 in both, 13,988 only before and 16,528 only after (@tbl-fixedmodel).
That is 34% of the flags before and 38% of those after, and 40-45% at genus and species level against 12-20% at phylum to family level.
Of the 26,599 flags in both, 11,075 propose another lineage.
The flags found in only one run do not have low placement weights here: the median is 1.0 in all three groups (shared, only before, only after), and 19% of the flags in either only-one group have a weight below 0.6, against 58% at 0.97.
The change is therefore not a matter of flags near the threshold.
A cause that fits is that the tree at 1.0 holds many nearly identical sequences, so which of them a sequence is placed next to, and so which species it is given, depends on small differences that the model changes.
That has not been tested.

Memory and time are unchanged by the model: one fold needs 135.6 GB and 4.5 minutes at 0.97 and 414.6 GB at 1.0 (47.5 minutes against 42.1; the first 1.0 run's folds ran alone).
The scoring step needs 35.9 GB at 0.97, and at 1.0 11.3 GB against 2.5 GB.
The placement tree is identical in each pair (same md5), so the seed reproduces the divided tree search.
The reference tree of the export differs because it is built after the flagged sequences are removed.

The comparisons with the divided placement are made against the rerun, so the model confound is removed for the parts (the shares moved by at most 5 points), but not for the backbone.
**Noise of the placement.**
To see what a repeat does without a model change, fold 0 of the 0.97 run under the correct model (3,697 queries) was placed again with the same input and container, at 8 instead of 12 threads (`scripts/large/noise.sh`, `jp.py`).
The file differs, but only slightly: the tree is the same, all 3,697 queries have the same top placement weight, and 3,641 (98.5%) have the same top edge.
All 56 queries with another top edge are ties between edges of equal weight, and 4 queries (0.1%) have another set of edges.
Ties are 2.5% of the queries of this fold, and 7.6% and 11.9% in the two folds of the 1.0 rerun that were counted (`scripts/large/ties.py`).
If ties are resolved differently as often at 1.0 as here (56 of 91), 5-7% of the queries of a 1.0 fold could change their top edge.
This is far below the 34-38% of the flags that differ between the models, but it is not negligible, and it is one fold at one cluster identity with a changed thread count.
A repeat of one 1.0 fold under the same model and thread count would settle it (48 minutes and 415 GB).

# Discussion

**Clustering to 0.97 is a trade-off, not a free saving.**
It makes one placement fold about 10 times shorter and 3 times lighter in memory at the price of about a third of the genus-level flags and two thirds of the species-level flags (@tbl-clustering, @tbl-099).
Which loss matters depends on the use: at phylum level the flags it drops mostly look wrong, at genus and species level they cannot be judged.
Going below 0.97 saves little (@tbl-sweep).
Going from 0.97 to 0.99 costs 12% more memory and 24% more time per fold and gives more species-level flags (42% of the representatives against 29%), so 0.99 is a middle choice if species-level flags matter and 1.0 is too expensive (@tbl-099).

**raxtax should stay on.**
The prefilter removes sequences that would otherwise create flags on their neighbours, and the flags it makes alone are mostly wrong where BLAST can say (@tbl-raxtax).

**Dividing the tree does not pay.**
The main reason is that a sequence's correct taxon is often not in its part, and that species flags depend on the wider tree (@tbl-divided).
A backbone stage recovers phylum to family flags but not genus flags, and it makes 4.7% false flags on control sequences (@tbl-backbone).
Each design would add considerable complexity to the pipeline for a gain in memory only, which clustering already provides.
The designs were not built into the pipeline.

**The model matters most for species-level flags at 1.0.**
Under the correct model the 1.0 run flags 6% more sequences, but only 62% of its flags are in the first run (@tbl-fixedmodel).
Species-level flags among near-identical sequences are the least reproducible, and a user should not expect the same flags from a different model, and placements that tie on weight can change between repeats.
The conclusions on clustering and on the divided parts hold against both versions of the benchmark.

**Limits.**
Each result is one run on one data set with one seed.
The BLAST check cannot judge flags with weak hits (about half of those tried) and does not judge species-level flags; the raxtax comparison and the genus- and species-level analyses of the parts were made on the first runs.
The divided tests sample 40 of 472 parts.
Long-branch attraction is a hypothesis for the artefactual phylum-level flags and has not been tested.
The scoring step's memory (35.9 GB at 92,406 sequences, 1.1 GB at 103,225, 11.3 GB at 239,806), the differences between the alignment-derived and the original sequences, and what profile cover removes are not explained.

**Open.**
The run-to-run noise was measured on one 0.97 fold only: a repeat of a 1.0 fold under the same model and thread count would show whether ties are resolved differently often enough to matter for flags.
The link from changed top edges to changed flags was not followed through the scoring step.
The backbone against the rerun is not done, nor are the raxtax comparison and the genus- and species-level analyses of the parts under the correct model.
